caption: The drawing is composed of brown ink on a cream-colored or yellowed plain background. It contains a rectangular box at the upper portion of the page, filled with handwritten Spanish text in a decorative, old-style script. The rectangular box is bordered by a line of small dots. Within the borders above and around the text are small clustered motifs resembling bunches of grapes or berries, repeated as a pattern. Below the main text box is a second, larger rectangular box outlined with a dotted border, which contains grape or berry cluster motifs at its outer edges and inside, with two vertical rows of these motifs running along its sides and a line of small glyph-like symbols at its bottom. Below this section, hanging from the lower edge of the larger box, is a large, branched vine structure, drawn with many curved lines bearing numerous grape or berry clusters and leaves, spreading widely to fill the lower part of the page. The entire composition uses only one color of ink, and the objects are all rendered in fine, consistent line work. There are no areas of solid shading or heavy cross-hatching, and the forms are stylized and decorative. In the top center, above the text, is a small cross-like motif. The page number "3" is printed in blue in the lower left corner.
title: Plate 3: Pecos Book of Visitations: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
